# Generated by `cargo run -p agent_docs` from the diagnostic registry and compiler/tests/ui; do not edit.
title: "W5005 linear_contract_on_hot_path"
description: "A requires, ensures, where or property requires clause calls List.all, List.any, List.contains or String.contains on a parameter (or it), so every check scans the whole value (design §7.2, §17.72)."
---

A warning from the `contract` phase. `sakura explain W5005` prints this explanation offline.

A `requires`, `ensures`, `where` or `property requires` clause calls `List.all`, `List.any`,
`List.contains` or `String.contains` on a parameter (or `it`), so every check scans the whole
value (design §7.2, §17.72). One warning per clause; std is exempt. Keep the clause when a linear
check is what you want, or move the invariant into a refined type so it is checked once, where
values are introduced.

Warning:

```sakura
fn total(xs: List<Int>) -> Int
  requires List.all(xs, fn(x) { x > 0 })
{ List.sum(xs) }
```

Fixed (the invariant is a type):

```sakura
type Positive = Int where it > 0
fn total(xs: List<Positive>) -> Int { List.fold(xs, 0, fn(acc, x) { acc + x }) }
```

## Wrong program

[`compiler/tests/ui/W5005_linear_contract_on_hot_path.sak`](https://github.com/icantcodefyi/sakuralang/blob/main/compiler/tests/ui/W5005_linear_contract_on_hot_path.sak), which the compiler's ui suite runs through `sakura check`:

```sakura
fn count_positive(xs: List<Int>) -> Int
  requires List.all(xs, fn(x) { x > 0 })
{ List.len(xs) }

fn many(xs: List<Int>) -> Int {
  var n = 0
  for _ in 0..1000 { n = n + count_positive(xs) }
  n
}
```

## Fixed program

[`compiler/tests/ui/W5005_linear_contract_on_hot_path.fixed.sak`](https://github.com/icantcodefyi/sakuralang/blob/main/compiler/tests/ui/W5005_linear_contract_on_hot_path.fixed.sak), which `sakura check` accepts with no diagnostics:

```sakura
type Positive = Int where it > 0

fn count_positive(xs: List<Positive>) -> Int { List.len(xs) }

fn many(xs: List<Positive>) -> Int {
  var n = 0
  for _ in 0..1000 { n = n + count_positive(xs) }
  n
}
```
